chunks: They are a people whom honour has always followed till they were made to settle in the house of eternal abode, and they obtained rest from the movement of journeying.

O listener! If you busy yourself in advancing towards these wonderful scenes which will rush towards you, then your heart will certainly die due to eagerness for them, and you will be prepared to seek the company of those in the graves straight away from my audience here and hasten towards them.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْقُبُورِ: People of the graves / Inhabitants of Barzakh
key_terms.دَارَ الْقَرَارِ: House of eternal abode / Permanent dwelling
key_terms.نُقْلَةَ الْأَسْفَارِ: Movement of journeying / Transitions of travel

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of contemplating the 'house of eternal abode' in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this passage from the 'Magnificence of the Creator in birds' sermon, Sharif al-Radi presents a vivid eschatological vision where the righteous, particularly the Ahl al-Bayt, have secured their permanent abode in Jannah, free from the transience of worldly travel. The rhetorical exhortation to the listener emphasizes *tadabbur* (contemplation) as a spiritual catalyst, urging the heart to internalize these divine scenes so intensely that the soul eagerly anticipates leaving the current worldly assembly for the eternal company of the graves. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the intercessory status of the Imams and the transformative power of spiritual longing (*shawq*) in preparing the believer for the Hereafter.
